english.title: Knowingly require another person to perform forced / compulsory labour
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) required another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE OTHER PERSON..), to perform forced or compulsory labour in circumstances, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CIRCUMSTANCES..), when you knew or ought to have known that

(A)_[he]_
(B)_[she]_

was being required to perform such labour
english.legislation: Contrary to section 71(1)(b) and (3) of the Coroners and Justice Act 2009.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required

english.notes: References to requiring a person to perform forced or compulsory labour are to be construed in accordance with Article 4 of the Human Rights Convention (which prohibits a person being required to perform forced or compulsory labour).

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Fourteen years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit on Prosecutions:
None.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
